title: A matrix representation for row and column operations
stem: The outer product of two vectors $A=(a_0,\ldots,a_{n-1})$ and $B=(b_0,\ldots,b_{n-1})$ defines $C_{ij}=a_i b_j$. Which listed representation is most suitable when C must be stored in correspondence with the vectors at arbitrary dimension n and matrix addition and multiplication should be straightforward?
options: A circular singly linked list with a head node whose heads are also linked in a list.
A circular singly linked list with a head node.
solution: The question asks for a matrix representation supporting matrix operations, not merely evaluating one entry of a rank-one formula. Orthogonal links organize every represented entry in both its row and column, providing the two traversal directions needed to combine corresponding rows and columns. A row-list hierarchy organizes rows but lacks an explicit column chain. The one-chain choices organize only one successor relation. Thus option 2 is the most suitable listed general matrix representation. Factorized storage of A and B can be smaller for the single outer product, but arbitrary addition is not closed within one outer product and factorization is not among the listed choices. This is a suitability judgment under the question’s general-operation requirement, not a claim that no other representation can perform matrix arithmetic. The answer is independently reasoned; no official key was available.

title: Recursive reverse-stride copying
stem: Copy every other element of an $N$-element array `a`, starting at its last element, into array `b` from index zero upward. Call `store(N-1,0)`. Which pseudocode is correct? Syntax below treats parameters as integers and arrays as available in the procedure.
solution: At call depth t, source rank must be $N-1-2t$ and destination rank t. Option 1 maintains both indices and stops once the source becomes negative, giving $\lceil N/2\rceil$ writes. Option 2 starts at b[1] and leaves b[0] unwritten. Option 3 copies every element rather than every other element. Option 4 advances the destination by an extra two between calls, in addition to its post-increment behavior, leaving gaps. All source options have the same negative-source stopping guard. Missing parameter declarations are not treated as a compilable-C test. The answer is independently derived, not an official key.
